question: E4b: does the rain of the last hours of the issue day, its peak intensity and its number of wet hours (hourly AORC rain, an analysis made after the fact) - information the daily total hides - and the flow relative to the basin's own Q95 make the all-river LSTM warn of more of the flood onsets 1 day ahead, and in particular of the onsets with little rain on the target day?

outcome: Given the rain of the last 3, 6 and 12 hours of the issue day, its wettest hour (basin mean and wettest 1 km cell) and its number of wet hours (hourly AORC rain, an analysis made after the fact) as six extra inputs beside the AORC rain to midnight to the LSTM with the river gauge, onsets warned 1 day ahead go from 51% with the AORC rain to midnight alone (hindsight at most about 3 points) to 56% (single trainings 50% to 58%; the onsets of one storm are not independent): +4.4 points over that model (340 against 313 hits of 611) and +2.9 points over the control with the same six columns one day older (53%); the share of false warnings among the onset warnings is 50% against 50% (the control: 56%); the median NSE goes from 0.77 to 0.77 (the seed-averaged forecast; single trainings 0.69 to 0.77); the verdict of results/flood_analysis.json is NOT YET for the onsets and CAUTION for all high-flow days.
outcome_caveat: The success rule fixed before training (wqaW above wqa and above wqaW_older in every seed at lead 1) is not met: the five single trainings with the within-day columns span 50.2% to 58.3% against 48.6% to 55.3% with the AORC rain to midnight alone and 48.8% to 53.8% for the older control; the control is flat on onsets warned (53% against 51%) and noisier (56% false against 50%; median NSE 0.74 against 0.77); 66 onsets are warned only with the within-day columns against 39 only without them. The Q95-relative flow alone (wqaQ) gives 52% (single trainings 49% to 55%) with a lower median NSE (0.73 against 0.77) and 53% false warnings (against 50%). In the 220 onsets with under 5 mm of AORC rain on the target day the share warned goes from 80% to 72% (older control 81%), in the 391 others from 35% to 47%: the gain sits in the wetter onsets, the opposite of the expectation of NEXT_EXPERIMENTS_2026-10-28.md. The gap in onsets warned from the AORC rain to midnight (51%) to the perfect rain forecast in the slots (wqaP, 66%, an upper bound that cannot be had in practice) is 14.9 points; the six columns move the share by +4.4 points and close 30% of it; in median NSE the gap is 0.029 and the move +0.003 (11% of it). At the warning level chosen on the validation years for onsets (0.95 against 1.00) wqaW warns of 60% with 53% false against 51% with 50% false; at the 30%-false operating point (the trigger chosen on the validation years so that at most 30% of the onset warnings are false: 1.50) it warns of 31% with 30% false on the test years, against 25% with 30% false for the AORC rain to midnight alone (trigger 1.60) and 30% with 31% false for the older control (trigger 1.45): at this operating point the six columns add nothing over the control. AORC is an analysis made after the fact: the within-day columns share the hindsight channel of the AORC rain to midnight (one factor per gauge day); the bound of that caveat (hindsight at most about 3 points) was measured for the daily total, not for these columns; they are a bound on what a real-time hourly rain product could add, not a service. The networks learned the within-day columns on hours that are daily totals spread by older products (all training years, 1980 to 2000, lie before 2002) and were scored on Stage IV-shaped hours; what this does to the gain was not measured. Every number of the new sets is a five-seed number; the stored sets have three seeds. With the substituted GEFS forecast beside them (wqaWF_sub against the stored wqaF_sub) onsets warned 1 day ahead go from 45% to 42% (single trainings 37% to 49%; false 33% against 35%; median NSE 0.72 against 0.69; 34 onsets warned only with the within-day columns against 52 only without them), at 2 and 3 days from 39% to 33% (15 onsets warned only with the within-day columns against 70 only without them) and from 37% to 34% (19 onsets warned only with the within-day columns against 56 only without them): by the seed rule 'no clear difference' at every lead; by the paired counts the within-day columns cost onsets at 2 and 3 days.

design.what: one LSTM (flood.LSTMNet, hidden 64) for all 12 basins with the river gauge (log1p flow) and the basin properties (flood.STATIC), the settings of results/lstm_all.json chosen there on the validation years; every set differs from wqa only in the daily input columns listed; the trainer stops on the mean validation NSE; the test years 2005-2014 are scored once

wqaQ.what: wqa + q_rel = log1p(q_mm / Q95): the flow of day t relative to the basin's own high-flow level (isolates the scaling change; the flow itself is an input of every set)

wqaW.what: wqa + the six within-day columns of the issue day (the test)

wqaW_older.what: wqa + the same six columns one day older: on issue day t the network reads the within-day columns of day t-1 (the same parameters, no new information about day t)

wqaWF_sub.what: wqaW + the substituted forecast columns fs1..fs3 of script 18 (trained on the AORC rain of the target days, stopped and scored with the bias-corrected GEFS forecast); compared with the stored lstm_wqaF_sub

wqa.what: the LSTM with the river gauge and the AORC rain to midnight (E1b): the base of every comparison here

wqaF_sub.what: wqa + the substituted GEFS forecast columns (E2a): the base of wqaWF_sub

wqaP.what: wqa + the AORC rain of the three target days in the slots: a perfect rain forecast, the ceiling (an upper bound that cannot be had in practice)

design.success_rule: wqaW above wqa and above wqaW_older in every seed at lead 1: onsets warned 1 day ahead, pooled over the 12 basins at trigger 1.0, every single seed of wqaW above every single seed of lstm_wqa (stored, three seeds) and of lstm_wqaW_older

columns.aorc_to_midnight: mm: the AORC rain of the whole local wall-clock day t (00:00 to 24:00 at the gauge, summer time included; the column of script 16, built here by code/subdaily_inputs.py and proved against it by a second route)
columns.aorc_last3h: mm: the AORC rain of the hours ending 22:00, 23:00 and 24:00 of day t (the last 3 hours before the issue time)
columns.aorc_last6h: mm: the AORC rain of the hours ending 19:00 to 24:00 of day t (the last 6 hours)
columns.aorc_last12h: mm: the AORC rain of the hours ending 13:00 to 24:00 of day t (the last 12 hours)
columns.aorc_max1h: mm: the wettest hour of day t (basin mean of the 1 km cells)
columns.aorc_maxcell1h: mm: the wettest 1 km cell in any hour of day t; NaN where every hour of the day was filled from ERA5 (max_cell_mm is NaN on filled hours) and then filled with aorc_max1h; raised to aorc_max1h on partly filled days where it sat below it (maxcell_fill_days)
columns.aorc_wet_hours: count: hours of day t with at least 0.5 mm of basin-mean rain
columns.q_rel: log1p(q_mm / Q95): the daily mean flow of day t relative to the basin's high-flow level (Q95 of its training years, flood.thresholds); the engine also reads log1p(q_mm) scaled by one global mean and spread
columns.older: the same six columns one day older: on issue day t the network reads the within-day columns of day t-1 (the first day keeps its own value, as the _older controls of scripts 10, 15 and 16)
columns.fs: fs1..fs3: the AORC rain of the local days t+1..t+3 for the issue days up to 2000-09-30, the bias-corrected GEFS control-member forecast of the same days from 2000-10-01 (the substituted table of script 18)
columns.hourly_shape: AORC's hours before 2002 are daily totals spread over the hours by the shape of older radar, satellite or model products (AORC v1.1 methods, as read by the E1b review); from 2002 they have Stage IV's hourly shape. The training years 1980-10 to 2000-09 all lie before 2002, the validation years 2000-2005 straddle the change, the test years 2005-2014 lie after it: the networks learned the six columns on hours of another source than the hours they were scored on; the effect on the gain was not measured (what_was_not_done)

forecast_columns.what: fs1..fs3: the AORC rain of the local days t+1..t+3 for the issue days up to 2000-09-30, the bias-corrected GEFS control-member forecast of the same days from 2000-10-01 (the substituted table of script 18)

maxcell_fill_days.what: filled_where_nan: days on which aorc_maxcell1h was NaN (every hour of the day filled from ERA5; max_cell_mm is NaN on filled hours) and was set to aorc_max1h; raised_to_max1h_on_partly_filled_days: days with some filled hours on which the cell maximum of the un-filled hours sat below the basin-mean wettest hour and was raised to it; per basin, as dates

summary_test.how_to_read: test years, seed average of each set, trigger 1.0, per lead; onset and all = warning tables pooled over the basins; the stored sets rescored here

validation_used_for_no_choice.label: USED FOR NO CHOICE. Validation years (2000-2005), shown for reference only: no set, setting or stopping point of this script was chosen on these scores (the settings came from 04_lstm_all.py; the trainer stopped each training on its own validation score, so these scores flatter the models). The validation years choose only the warning levels of verdicts and operating_points, which is labelled there.

per_basin.how_to_read: test years, one value per basin; the seed average of each set (flood.evaluate); gauge ids are text

seed_ranges.how_to_read: lowest and highest single-seed value of the test-year scores, per set and lead (by_seed: the single values, in the order of the seeds)

gain_rule.how_to_read: the checks of report section 4.2 for every pair (set T against set C): NSE clear gain = every seed of T above every seed of C, higher in most basins, Wilcoxon p below 0.05; onsets clear gain = every seed above every seed (pooled POD)

within_day_columns.what: the worth of the six within-day columns: lstm_wqaW minus lstm_wqa (the same inputs without them; stored, script 16)
within_day_columns.how_to_read: by_lead.l<k>: set T (with_set) minus set C (without_set) on the test years at trigger 1.0, seed-averaged forecasts; seed_range_* and every_seed_* use all seeds of each set; difference_by_seed_points and difference_by_seed pair the same seed number of both sets in order and cover only the seeds both sets have (seeds_paired; a five-seed set against a three-seed stored set gives three entries, seeds 3 and 4 of the new set are not in these lists); overlap_of_warned_onsets: the onsets warned by both sets, by only one, by neither

within_day_against_the_older_control.what: lstm_wqaW minus lstm_wqaW_older: the same six columns one day older (the same parameters, no new information about day t); the difference is what the hours of day t add
within_day_against_the_older_control.how_to_read: by_lead.l<k>: set T (with_set) minus set C (without_set) on the test years at trigger 1.0, seed-averaged forecasts; seed_range_* and every_seed_* use all seeds of each set; difference_by_seed_points and difference_by_seed pair the same seed number of both sets in order and cover only the seeds both sets have (seeds_paired; a five-seed set against a three-seed stored set gives three entries, seeds 3 and 4 of the new set are not in these lists); overlap_of_warned_onsets: the onsets warned by both sets, by only one, by neither

older_control_against_wqa.what: is the control flat? lstm_wqaW_older minus lstm_wqa: six more columns that hold nothing about day t (if they are not above the seeds of wqa, the control is flat)
older_control_against_wqa.how_to_read: by_lead.l<k>: set T (with_set) minus set C (without_set) on the test years at trigger 1.0, seed-averaged forecasts; seed_range_* and every_seed_* use all seeds of each set; difference_by_seed_points and difference_by_seed pair the same seed number of both sets in order and cover only the seeds both sets have (seeds_paired; a five-seed set against a three-seed stored set gives three entries, seeds 3 and 4 of the new set are not in these lists); overlap_of_warned_onsets: the onsets warned by both sets, by only one, by neither

within_day_against_q_rel.how_to_read: by_lead.l<k>: set T (with_set) minus set C (without_set) on the test years at trigger 1.0, seed-averaged forecasts; seed_range_* and every_seed_* use all seeds of each set; difference_by_seed_points and difference_by_seed pair the same seed number of both sets in order and cover only the seeds both sets have (seeds_paired; a five-seed set against a three-seed stored set gives three entries, seeds 3 and 4 of the new set are not in these lists); overlap_of_warned_onsets: the onsets warned by both sets, by only one, by neither

how_far_from_perfect_rain.what: lstm_wqaW minus lstm_wqaP (the AORC rain of the target days in the slots: a perfect rain forecast, an upper bound that cannot be had in practice): what the within-day rain of day t cannot reach

paired_onsets.how_to_read: per pair and lead: the onsets of the test years warned by both sets, by only one, by neither (flood.flood_scores' onsets at trigger 1.0; the sign test is a description, the onsets of one storm are not independent)

little_rain_onsets.what: lead 1, main split: the 611 onsets of the test years sliced by the rain of the target day and of the issue day (AORC rain to midnight, Daymet rain), with the share each set warned of at the fixed level (seed-averaged forecasts; single_seeds = lowest and highest single seed), the paired counts, and where the gain of wqaW sits. Read from the saved sets and the tables; nothing is trained

aorc_target_below_5mm.rule: AORC rain of the target day below 5 mm (the rule of script 18's lead1_facts: results/forecast_input.json, lead1_facts.little_rain_on_the_target_day)

aorc_target_at_least_5mm.rule: AORC rain of the target day at least 5 mm

daymet_target_below_5mm.rule: Daymet rain stamped on the target day below 5 mm (the rain table's day ends at about 09:00, so this is mostly the rain of the night before the target day)

daymet_target_at_least_5mm.rule: Daymet rain stamped on the target day at least 5 mm

aorc_issue_day_below_1mm.rule: AORC rain of the issue day below 1 mm (the onsets the work order says need the forecast or the river's state, not within-day rain)

aorc_issue_day_at_least_1mm.rule: AORC rain of the issue day at least 1 mm

aorc_last6h_of_issue_day_at_least_5mm.rule: at least 5 mm of AORC rain in the last 6 hours of the issue day (where the within-day columns hold the most)

aorc_last6h_of_issue_day_below_5mm.rule: under 5 mm of AORC rain in the last 6 hours of the issue day

where_the_gain_sits.what: where the hit gain of wqaW over wqa sits: inside the slice of onsets with under 5 mm of AORC rain on the target day and outside it (hits of the seed-averaged forecasts)

closure.how_to_read: the share of the gap from the base to the ceiling (lstm_wqaP, the perfect rain forecast in the slots) that each set closes, per lead, in median NSE and in onsets warned

operating_points.how_to_read: per set and lead, two triggers chosen on the validation years by code/warning_policy.choose_trigger over its grid (0.50 to 2.00 step 0.05) and scored once on the test years: csi (best pooled onset CSI, the project's rule) and far_cap (highest pooled onset POD with pooled onset FAR at most 0.30 on validation; reached=false means no trigger of the grid met the cap on validation and the lowest-FAR trigger is given). e4b_success.rule: wqaW above wqa and above wqaW_older in every seed at lead 1: onsets warned 1 day ahead, pooled over the 12 basins at trigger 1.0, every single seed of wqaW above every single seed of lstm_wqa (stored, three seeds) and of lstm_wqaW_older

expected_where.what: NEXT_EXPERIMENTS_2026-10-28.md (E4b) and the work order expect the gain in the onsets with under 5 mm of rain on the target day (results/review_forecast_input.json, must_fix[0] (iv)); this is a description, not part of the rule; expectation_met and reading say whether it held
expected_where.reading: the gain sits in the wetter onsets, the opposite of the expectation of NEXT_EXPERIMENTS_2026-10-28.md

causality.what: (1) data side: code/subdaily_inputs.checks() on the real series (data_side); (2) engine: flood.fit runs flood._assert_causal on every network before training (random inputs: a change after day T/2 must not change the output before it; a trained network exists only if it passed); (3) end to end: the made-up-values test on one SAVED network per set (first seed): the set's new columns (and in a second round every input column and the flow) of all days after a cut day were replaced by random values (0 to 120 per day); no forecast issued on or before the cut day changed (exactly equal, all three leads, all 12 basins) and the forecasts issued after it did; (4) the within-day columns are dated by the ISSUE day t and hold hours ending at or before 24:00 of day t, so a forecast issued on t reads only hours up to the issue time (data_side); the _older columns hold day t-1

data_side.what: Checks of code/subdaily_inputs.py and the timing of the issue-day rain before the test-year onsets (written 2026-10-29)
data_side.how: code/subdaily_inputs.checks(): per basin the two routes to the daily total agree, the window sums are in order (3 h <= 6 h <= 12 h <= day), every day has 23, 24 or 25 hours, and the made-up-hours test (every hour after the issue time of a cut day x7+100: no row up to the cut day moves, the next day moves) passed; its record is rewritten to results/diagnostics_2026-10-28/subdaily_inputs_check.json
data_side.note: the rain-timing statistic of that diagnostic (issue_day_rain_timing_test_years) is not carried into this file: it is a preliminary diagnostic, not a result of this experiment

causality.engine_check: flood._assert_causal at the start of every flood.fit (asserted: a trained network exists only if it passed)

reload_check.what: one trained network per set (the first seed) rebuilt from its .pt file alone (flood.LSTMNet + the saved weights, settings and scalers), run on the same tables, and compared with the forecasts stored by save_preds
reload_check.tolerance: numpy.allclose, rtol 1e-6, atol 1e-8, missing values equal; same machine (the networks of the stored sets, trained on the Mac, are not reloaded here)

integrity.how_to_read: sha256 of every prediction set and network file of this script, as they are when this file is written; made_in_this_pass lists the files this pass wrote; every other file was only read. A later pass compares the hashes of the files it only reads with these and stops if one differs. stored_sets_read: the files of the stored comparison sets as read (never written by this script).

choices_made_after_looking_at_test_score: The sets wqaQ, wqaW and wqaWF_sub, the scoring (as script 16: seed rule, paired onsets, per-basin, the closure of the gap to wqaP; and the 30%-false operating point of E4a) and the expectation (the gain in the onsets with little rain on the target day) were fixed in NEXT_EXPERIMENTS_2026-10-28.md; the older control wqaW_older, the success rule as worded (wqaW above wqa and above wqaW_older in every seed at lead 1) and the five seeds were fixed in this script before the first training (its sha256 is recorded at the start of every pass: 9b7026ae565bdc84f266e64239b4698c77a165907f26f00a14d77c1744b2ead0 for the training pass, passes[0].script_sha256); the test years were scored once.
One training pass (finished 2026-10-29 00:02) went straight to five seeds per set; no --extend pass exists.

passes.what: training run: every set from scratch
rescore (--rescore): scores, tables, outcome and figure recomputed from the saved sets, nothing trained

notes: aorc_maxcell1h was filled with aorc_max1h on 13 basin-days whose every hour was filled from ERA5 and raised to aorc_max1h on 2 partly filled basin-days (maxcell_fill_days); aorc_filled_hours is the quality flag and is not an input.

The stored sets lstm_wqa, lstm_wqaF_sub and lstm_wqaP were rescored by this script's code from results/preds (checks_against_stored_results proves the same numbers as their own results files); their networks, trained on the Mac, were not reloaded here (a cross-machine reload is not expected to pass rtol 1e-6).

The simple-model yardstick (ridge regression and the random forest given the within-day columns, rule 2 of the work order) was not run: the engine audit of 2026-10-28 made it optional for the deadline; the hourly columns would need an extension of features.py.

Quoting. Any document must quote outcome_full (outcome plus outcome_caveat), never outcome alone; every number is a seed-averaged number unless it says 'single trainings'; the status field says whether the experiment has been reviewed.

212 values in this file are null: a number that is not finite (NaN: a share whose denominator is zero, a p-value that is not defined, the load average, which Windows does not have; 0 of them NaN in this pass's own numbers, the others null already in what this pass read back from the earlier pass) or a value that does not exist. A reader must treat null as 'no value'.
